title: Start and stop a motor
brief: Press Start and the motor runs, and keeps running after you let go. Press Stop and it stops. The Stop button is wired normally closed: its input is TRUE while nobody is pressing it.
hints: A coil is only on while power reaches it. What keeps power flowing after you let go of Start?
Put a contact for the Motor tag in parallel with the Start contact. This is called a seal-in (or holding) contact.
The Stop input is TRUE while Stop is not pressed, so a normally open contact for Stop passes power until someone presses it.

scenarios.name: Start runs the motor, and it keeps running

assertions.says: The motor should be running 0.1 s after Start is pressed.
The motor should keep running after Start is released.
The motor should be running after Start.
The motor should stop 0.1 s after Stop is pressed.
The motor should stay stopped after Stop is released.
With Stop held down, Start must not run the motor.
